tools.description: Start rendering a composition range (or a media-bin asset range with aliasId) to sampled frames + optional MP4; returns the resultId it will publish (poll previewVideoStatus, then fetch previewVideoFrames by id) [inspection]

maxWidth.description: Maximum output width in pixels (default 720, max 1920)

aliasId.description: Media-bin asset aliasId: render that asset's source range instead of the timeline

startSeconds.description: Range start in seconds (default: playhead, or 0 with aliasId)

sourceStartSeconds.description: Asset source start in seconds; with aliasId, overrides startSeconds (default 0)

includeClip.description: Also encode a trimmed MP4 clip (default true)

clipMaxWidth.description: Maximum clip width in pixels for the MP4 encode only; sampled frames keep using maxWidth (default: maxWidth; clamped 160-1920, disclosed as requestedClipMaxWidth + clamped when moved). Average-bitrate clips target a 6 MiB (6291456-byte) budget, not a hard guarantee. When enabled, constant quality uses the configured export quality level. After encoding, previewVideoStatus verifies the actual sizeBytes and adds clipOverBudget: true + maxClipBytes to the clip entry only when it exceeds that budget (e.g. at the 400 kbps bitrate floor). Use a smaller clipMaxWidth (e.g. 540 for 10s) for reliably smaller clips. GET /previewVideo/clip serves the clip as raw binary and is Mac-local / agent-channel-unsafe; base64 clip delivery is EB-17's job, not this parameter.

tools.name: previewVideoFrames
tools.description: Fetch a finished previewVideo render's frames by resultId [inspection]

resultId.description: Result id returned by the previewVideo POST and previewVideoStatus. Finished results are retained (max 4, up to 16 MiB of frame data, oldest evicted first); an unknown or evicted id returns an explicit error.

includeFrames.description: Return the old full shape ({result: ...} with inline base64 frames and clip metadata). Default (omitted/false): only lightweight fields — rendering, resultId, ok, error, frameCount, start, duration and the finished result's other small metadata (projectId, compositionDuration, visualDuration, mode, aliasId, clip) — no frame bytes. Fetch frames once via GET /previewVideoFrames?resultId=...
